ca_hoodgie_wall.blurb: Hoodgie Wall is a stand-alone formation in the Alabama Hills near Lone Pine, on the Eastern Sierra side of California, and one of the crags grouped under the Western Wall Area. It has eight routes, split evenly between bolted sport lines and trad lines, all in the moderate range from 5.6 up to 5.9. Most of the climbing is on a clean slab, with a few additional lines on a second face. With grades this friendly it works as a short stop for climbers building up on easier sport and trad leads.

ca_i_below_smooth_sole_wall_face.blurb: Below Smooth Sole Wall Face sits on Suicide Rock above Idyllwild, directly beneath the larger Smooth Sole Wall. It has eight routes, mostly trad with two bolted sport lines, spanning 5.8 to 5.12, with the bulk of them around 5.10. The wall takes sun for most of the day, so it can run warm on bright afternoons. Suicide Rock as a whole leans toward traditional leads, and bolted lines here still tend to ask for steady nerves.

ca_inauguron_dome.blurb: Inauguron Dome is a large west-facing formation at the southern end of Secret Valley, in the Wonderland of Rocks section of Joshua Tree National Park. Its eight routes are mostly trad, plus one top-rope line, ranging from an easy 5.3 up to 5.11, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.11. Several climbs run two pitches on face and crack terrain, and the bolted face lines can still call for extra gear, so bring a full rack. Facing west, the wall picks up the afternoon sun. It is reached on foot up Wonderland Valley.

ca_johnny_wall.blurb: Johnny Wall is a small top-rope wall in the Indian Springs area along Eagle Lakes Road in the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe. It stands across from the campground entrance, set about 100 feet back among the trees and partly hidden from view. All eight climbs are top-rope lines with bolt anchors at the top, running from 5.5 to 5.9 with most around 5.7. That spread makes it a convenient place for beginners or for teaching, and a quick session when staying at the campground.

ca_charlotte_dome.blurb: Charlotte Dome is a High Sierra backcountry dome just past Charlotte Lake, reached on foot from either the Cedar Grove or the Kearsarge Pass trailhead, so plan a backpacking trip rather than a day outing. Its eight routes are long trad and alpine-style lines graded from 5.7 to 5.11, with the longest running about twelve pitches. Campsites are available beneath the dome. Expect a big, committing day on the wall after a substantial walk in.

ca_keystone_block.blurb: Keystone Block is a small formation in the Barker Dam Area of central Joshua Tree National Park, with parking at the Barker Dam Loop trailhead. The block sits in the canyon that separates Dissolution Rock from Hunk Rock, and can be spotted up and to the right as you walk in. It has eight routes, mostly trad with two top-rope lines, from 5.6 up to 5.10, with most of the grades between 5.7 and 5.10. That range gives beginners and intermediate climbers a handful of options in one stop.

ca_lambada_dome_left.blurb: Lambada Dome Left is a west-facing slab in the Little Egypt area near Bishop, in the Eastern Sierra. It has eight routes, five trad and three sport, from 5.8 to 5.11, with most at 5.10. The climbing follows a dark patina slab. The wall stays in shade until about late morning, then takes direct afternoon sun, so summer afternoons can run hot. The walk in takes roughly half an hour from the parking area.
